review_note: Independent mathematical comparison with pinned original statement in Stage A sites.tex:5637. Did not view any proof or unsafe source slice. A compatible collection of sheaf maps over a covering U_i→U glues uniquely over the slice C/U. The overlap condition is equality after restricting to the pairwise fibre-product site and the conclusion is a unique global map whose restrictions recover each local map; the slogan alone was removed.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\{U_i \to U\}$ be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ be sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$.
Given a collection
$$
\varphi_i :
\mathcal{F}|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i}
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{G}|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i}
$$
of maps of sheaves such that for all $i, j \in I$ the maps
$\varphi_i, \varphi_j$ restrict to the same map
$\varphi_{ij} : \mathcal{F}|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i \times_U U_j} \to
\mathcal{G}|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i \times_U U_j}$
then there exists a unique map of sheaves
$$
\varphi :
\mathcal{F}|_{\mathcal{C}/U}
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{G}|_{\mathcal{C}/U}
$$
whose restriction to each $\mathcal{C}/U_i$ agrees with $\varphi_i$.

review_note: Independent mathematical comparison with pinned original statement in Stage A sites.tex:5716. Did not view any proof or unsafe source slice. The cartesian-closed adjunction Mor(F×G,H)≅Mor(F,SheafHom(G,H)) is stated as a natural bijection in all three sheaf variables. The prepared formulation preserves both the variance of internal Hom and functoriality and makes no unwarranted objectwise Hom claim.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ and
$\mathcal{H}$ be sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$. There is a canonical bijection
$$
\Mor_{\Sh(\mathcal{C})}(\mathcal{F}\times\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}) =
\Mor_{\Sh(\mathcal{C})}(\mathcal{F},\SheafHom(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}))
$$
which is functorial in all three entries.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-internal-hom-sheaf}
\begin{slogan}
The category of sheaves on a site is cartesian closed
\end{slogan}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ and
$\mathcal{H}$ be sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$. There is a canonical bijection
$$
\Mor_{\Sh(\mathcal{C})}(\mathcal{F}\times\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}) =
\Mor_{\Sh(\mathcal{C})}(\mathcal{F},\SheafHom(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}))
$$
which is functorial in all three entries.

review_note: Independent mathematical comparison with pinned original statement in Stage A sites.tex:5847. Did not view any proof or unsafe source slice. Given a site covering and arbitrary compatible glueing data (F_i,φ_ij), the source promises existence of a sheaf on C/U and isomorphisms to the F_i that satisfy the specified overlap squares. The quantified given data remain explicitly in the conclusion and Stage A does not invent uniqueness for this existential statement.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
Given any glueing data $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ij})$
for sheaves of sets with respect to the covering $\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
there exists a sheaf of sets $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}/U$
together with isomorphisms
$$
\varphi_i : \mathcal{F}|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i} \to \mathcal{F}_i
$$
such that the diagrams
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{F}|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i \times_U U_j}
\ar[d]_{\text{id}} \ar[r]_{\varphi_i} &
\mathcal{F}_i|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i \times_U U_j} \ar[d]^{\varphi_{ij}} \\
\mathcal{F}|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i \times_U U_j} \ar[r]^{\varphi_j} &
\mathcal{F}_j|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i \times_U U_j}
}
$$
are commutative.

review_note: Independent mathematical comparison with pinned original statement in Stage A sites.tex:5909. Did not view any proof or unsafe source slice. Sheaves on the slice site C/U are equivalent to the category of gluing data on the chosen covering. The source states equivalence via the canonical restriction-to-covering functor; the prepared statement keeps that functor and does not claim equality of categories.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
The category $\Sh(\mathcal{C}/U)$ is equivalent
to the category of glueing data via the functor that associates
to $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}/U$ the canonical glueing data.
